gloss: tail end; rear; end of the line

definitions.gloss: tail end; rear; very back of a line or procession
definitions.explanation: The very last position in a queue, procession, or sequence. Commonly used when referring to the end of a line of people waiting, or the rear of a group or formation.

examples.japanese: {最後尾|さいごび}はあちらです。
examples.english: The end of the line is over there.

examples.japanese: {最後尾|さいごび}に{並|なら}んでください。
examples.english: Please line up at the end of the line.

examples.japanese: {行列|ぎょうれつ}の{最後尾|さいごび}まで{歩|ある}いたら、{駅|えき}の{角|かど}を{曲|ま}がったところまで{続|つづ}いていた。
examples.english: When I walked to the end of the line, it extended around the corner of the station.

notes:
Combines {最後|さいご} (last) and {尾|び} (tail). The {尾|び} character reinforces the image of the very tail end — beyond merely being "last" ({最後|さいご}), {最後尾|さいごび} specifically indicates the physical end position.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {最後尾|さいごび}に{並|なら}ぶ: to line up at the back
- {最後尾|さいごび}の{人|ひと}: the person at the very back
- {最後尾|さいごび}{札|ふだ}: "end of line" sign (held by staff)
- {行列|ぎょうれつ}の{最後尾|さいごび}: end of a queue

USAGE:
Very commonly seen at popular restaurants, theme parks, event venues, and shops where queues form. Staff members often hold signs reading {最後尾|さいごび} to indicate where the line ends. The word carries a polite, somewhat formal register and is the standard term used in public signage.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {最後|さいご}: last — refers to the final item in a sequence, but does not specifically mean the physical end of a line
- {後方|こうほう}: rear — indicates the back area in general, not specifically the tail end of a queue
- {末尾|まつび}: end, tail — used for the end of a list or text, rarely for physical queues
